source_theorem: HARNESS-DIFFERENCE port, verified in a scratch suite (interp: PASS). In a registration function, a directly called nested function 'fn attempt() -> str errors std::compiler::CompilerError:' whose static compile block holds the offending registration: 'fn body() errors std::compiler::CompilerError:' with body 'std::test::count()', then 'std::test::value("nested", 0, body)', then the value "accepted". The registration function handles it: got = attempt(): on std::compiler::CompilerError {code}: std::test::code_name(code); a body whose block is just 'got' is registered with std::test::value("gf-body-cannot-use-context", "ContextFunctionValue", b). attempt is called, not used as a value, so it may require the Suite; the function-value use of body is inside the block, so ContextFunctionValue is that block's reified rejection.
notes: in the Tcl program the registration is outside any block and the whole program is rejected; a golden suite can observe that rejection only by moving the registration call into a block as above (an OUTER-ANCHOR otherwise). The Tcl test asserts only the kind (message glob '*'). Alternatively compare the code with == in the registration function and register a value test of the Bool.
